Name: Voliro
Description:
Voliro builds advanced aerial robots that don't just fly and see - they touch.

Born out of ETH Zurich's Autonomous Systems Lab, Voliro has pioneered a new category in industrial inspection: contact-based drone inspection. Our patented tiltable-rotor platform, the Voliro T, physically interacts with structures to perform Non-Destructive Testing (NDT), ultrasonic thickness measurements, and Lightning Protection System (LPS) inspections with no scaffolding, no rope access, no shutdowns required.

The Voliro T is equipped with interchangeable sensor payloads and AI-powered flight control, enabling pilots to inspect flare stacks, storage tanks, chimneys, wind turbines, and other critical assets while they remain in service.

With its tiltable rotor system, Voliro expands the abilities of service drones from “fly and see” to “fly, see and touch”. Voliro T, our flying robot, can be equipped with a variety of payloads, such as Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) or Lightning Protection System (LPS) sensors. The unique 360° drone design of Voliro T allows inspection of curved and sloped surfaces. No other flying inspection robot boasts these capabilities.

Voliro aims to provide innovative UAVs with unique capabilities. We promote the concept of an omnidirectional aerial robotic platform, where position and orientation of the flying platform are completely independent. This ability is crucial to achieve robust and reliable interaction with the environment.

Our mission: make the world's critical infrastructure safer, more reliable, and easier to maintain  without putting people at risk.

Name: Dark Cloud  Labs

Name: Fenyx Art
Description:
Founded in 2005 as a creative design studio, Fenyx Art began with a simple mission: helping individuals and organizations communicate through design, creativity and visual identity. 
The emergence of Artificial Intelligence in 2022 transformed not only the technological landscape, but also our understanding of creativity, knowledge and human-machine interaction. 

Today, Fenyx Art has evolved beyond traditional branding and design services. Our work focuses on Cognitive Architecture, Human-AI Governance and the design of meaning-oriented intelligent systems. We explore how artificial intelligences perceive reality, interpret information, construct meaning and interact with human beings. 

By combining artistic vision, systems thinking, philosophy, cybersecurity and emerging technologies, we help shape intelligent systems that are not only efficient, but also coherent, relevant and aligned with human values. 

We believe the future is not built with code alone. It is built through purpose, empathy, understanding and meaningful design.

Name: TrainIt Robotics
Description:
TrainIt Robotics is an Industrial Physical AI company developing adaptive robotic systems for High-Mix, Low-Volume production.

Traditional automation works well when products, positions and process conditions are known in advance. When formats change, objects arrive in random orientations, visual conditions vary or the process requires recovery from uncertainty, deterministic logic alone is no longer enough.

The PLC remains the deterministic backbone of the machine. TrainIt adds the adaptive layer: perception, decision-making, manipulation and recovery.

We design, simulate and deploy robotic applications that combine 6-axis industrial robots, integrated vision systems, digital twins, edge AI and PLC-connected software.

Our pipeline is:

DESIGN — We analyse the industrial task, product variability, cycle time, workspace, robot, camera, end effector and machine interfaces.

SIMULATION — We create a digital twin to validate reachability, collisions, camera positioning, cycle time and manipulation strategies. We evaluate and adapt Vision-Language-Action models, perception pipelines and proprietary trained skills to the customer’s process.

DEPLOYMENT — We integrate the robot, vision system, edge computer, end effector, application software and PLC communication into the real production environment.

Typical applications include bin picking, cap and capsule feeding, bottle and container handling, machine tending, robotic sorting, visual inspection, capping support, crating, nesting, de-nesting, packaging handling and palletizing.

We focus on beverage, food, cosmetics, pharmaceutical packaging and adjacent industrial sectors where variability makes rigid automation expensive or difficult to scale.

Instead of rebuilding every robotic project from scratch, we adapt reusable TrainIt skills to the customer’s objects, formats, equipment and production constraints.

Physical AI for Industrial Robotics.

Name: RIVR
Description: RIVR is a robotics company pioneering Physical AI for doorstep delivery. We combine neural networks with innovative wheeled-legged robots to automate the most labor-intensive part of delivery, bringing packages and food directly to consumers’ doorsteps, while mastering real-world challenges like climbing stairs, navigating cluttered spaces, and opening gates and doors. With customers already requiring tens of thousands of robots, RIVR is on track to generate more daily data than YouTube within four years, unlocking a powerful data flywheel for General Physical AI.

Name: CynLr
Description: CynLr is a visual object intelligence platform that enables industrial robotic arms to see, understand and manipulate any object in random unstructured environments.

Name: mimic
Description: Physical AI to scale your most tedious tasks from manufacturing to logistics. Our robots intuitively learn new skills from you and operate autonomously in any environment.

Name: microagi
Description: microagi, founded in 2025, is a robotics deployment company. Its platform, Atlas, fine-tunes models on a customer’s own operations, drawing on microagi’s proprietary data corpus, and closes the gap between the robot that impresses in a demo and the robot that does reliable work on the line. Atlas is hardware- and model-agnostic: a neutral layerbetween a customer’s infrastructure and frontier AI models, designed to prevent lock-in to any single vendor. microagi is headquartered in Munich, with a research hub in Zurich and offices in London and New York.

Name: Flexion
Description: We are building the autonomy stack for humanoid robots - from command to control, from manipulation to locomotion, across any hardware and task. Leveraging the power of simulation and reinforcement learning, our software scales to the real world with minimal human involvement.

Name: ETH Robotics Club
Description:
The ETH Robotics Club is a newly founded student organization at ETH Zurich, created by and for students with a shared passion for robotics.

Our goal is to build a community around hands-on learning and real-world systems in areas such as autonomous drones, humanoid robots, and dexterous manipulation. 

In just the first few months since our launch, we’ve made significant progress. We now count over 200 student members across diverse disciplines, reflecting the strong enthusiasm for robotics at ETH. We are proud to have invited renowned professors such as Marco Hutter and Raffaello D'Andrea to join our advisory board. We’ve also forged partnerships with industry leaders such as NVIDIA, OpenAI and Hugging Face, as well as ETH-affiliated robotics startups and global leaders in venture capital, helping us build strong connections with the broader robotics ecosystem.

We aim to offer students opportunities to learn, experiment, and collaborate on robotics challenges that go beyond the classroom. In time, we hope to grow into a hub for technical development, research collaboration, and student-led innovation.

If you’re a student, researcher, alumnus, or sponsor interested in robotics at ETH, we’d love to hear from you.

Description: An ETH-rooted company, Duatic develops and manufactures the Alpha, a high-performance, wheeled humanoid robot for industrial automation. Our systems, powered by proprietary Quasi-Direct Drive (QDD) technology, solve critical labor shortages by automating complex material handling and intralogistics in environments built for people. Name: roboa
Description:
When inspecting confined spaces, existing solutions struggle in winding, sharp, or slippery conditions.
roboa overcomes these limitations with its cutting-edge, snake-like robot, which uses growing-based locomotion to go where no human or other robot can go!

With exceptional maneuverability, roboa autonomously navigates and senses its environment, gathers vital maintenance data to reduce costly downtime, and improves safety.

Founded by ETH Zurich engineers, roboa is set to revolutionize industries like wastewater, chemicals, power, and oil and gas, making operations safer and more efficient.
Beyond industry, roboa supports search and rescue missions, where it locates and assists victims trapped under debris.

Contact us to learn more and discuss how we can work together!

Name: ETH RobotX
Description: The ETH+ initiative RobotX started in 2019 and has the ambition to position ETH (and Switzerland as a whole) at the top of robotics research institutions worldwide. The goal of this cross-departmental initiative of MAVT, ITET, INFK, USYS, MATL, ARCH, BAUG, and HEST is to develop the strong competences of ETH in robotics into a joint research and educational platform. RobotX will be located in the historical ML hall in the main campus of ETH providing large research and educational facilities. We will organize hands-on robot classes, annual summer schools and symposia, joint research programs with industry, and additional outreach programs to educate and host people from outside the ETH domain.

Name: Bubble Robotics
Description:
Bubble designs and operates fleets of integrated autonomous surface–subsea robotic systems that remain at sea for up to six months, delivering continuous inspection, survey, and underwater monitoring without ever sending vessels or crews to sea.

Our systems generate millimeter-resolution data, processed with AI to transform raw observations into actionable insights for infrastructure owners, operators, and public authorities. Compared to traditional offshore methods, Bubble delivers superior results at a fraction of the cost, with faster deployment and dramatically lower operational constraints.

By making industry-grade underwater data persistent, affordable, and on-demand, Bubble enables safer infrastructure, healthier ecosystems, and more resilient coastlines across the systems that power and protect life on Earth.

Name: Nautica Technologies
Description: Over 80% of world trade moves on vessels. At Nautica Technologies we are building the resilience layer for the world's fleet. Based in Zurich and backed by experienced VCs, we operate at the intersection of physical AI and data to solve critical challenges in the world's logistics backbone.

Name: Computational Robotics Lab - ETH Zürich
Description: We develop theoretical foundations to shape the way future generations of robots are made, how they operate in complex environments, and how they interact with us. In this quest, we define Computational Robotics as the fusion of simulation, algorithms and data. In brief, we formalize advanced simulation models to provide robots with an innate understanding of the laws of physics. Leveraging these models, we devise practical algorithms for motion planning, motion control and computational design problems. Whenever possible, we exploit data to efficiently learn solution spaces, to create faithful digital twins through real-to-sim methodologies, and to enable humans to teach robots new skills.

Name: Caterra
Description:
Today, the only alternative to herbicides in agriculture is a combination of mechanical hacking, flaming and hand weeding. To make scalable organic farming possible, technologies are needed that greatly reduce the use of manual labour.

Thanks to its laser-based approach Caterra’s robot allows the removal of weeds which are in close proximity to the crop, something mechanical methods are unable to do. Small, lightweight, fully electrical and chemical free!

SWOZI is a sports technology company with an extensive background in machine automation. We design, develop and manufacture the industry’s most versatile line marking system and applications for sports fields. Our pioneering solutions are based on cutting-edge GPS and robotic technology to simplify workflows for turf fields while meeting sporting code with 100% accuracy. Greenkeepers, line marking businesses and sports field operators all over the world trust our expertise.

Based on our knowledge and broad experience, SWOZI also undertakes engineering consultancy and projects where our core competency contributes to the success of external companies. Our focus here is on workflow optimisation for tasks where machine control can be involved.

Name: Multi-Scale Robotics Lab, ETH Zurich
Description: Projects at the Multi-Scale Robotics Lab are highly integrated, multi-disciplinary collaborations that aim to push the boundaries of current knowledge and broaden the scope of micro and nanoscale engineering. Our research examines topical problems in such diverse fields as microrobotically assisted surgery, magnetic actuation and manipulation, micro and nanofabrication, low Reynolds number locomotion, wireless delivery of power, electrostimulation of biological materials and micro and nanostructure characterization.

Name: FireDrone
Description: The FireDrone addresses the need for safe and efficient tools in extreme temperature environments such as firefighting and industrial inspection. Traditional drones fail in these environments, exposing workers to risks such as toxic smoke, structural collapse, and intense heat. The FireDrone is designed to withstand temperatures up to 200°C, enabling safe and rapid hazard detection and situational awareness. It enables users to increase safety, reduce operational downtime, and minimize environmental impact.

Name: REHAssist

Name: Equilibrio
Description:
Our Team
Equilibrio consists of 12 bachelor students from ETH Zürich in Mechanical and Electrical Engineering and from ZHAW in Systems Engineering. Supported by Prof. Dr. Marco Hutter and experienced tutors from the Robotic Systems Lab, we work together as an interdisciplinary team to develop an innovative robotic system.

Our Mission
Our goal is to build a robotic unicycle capable of driving not only on flat ground but also on uneven terrain. The robot will feature a wheel as its base, a actuated closed kinematic chain as a leg that enables it to jump, hip joints for dynamic balancing, and an upper body holding all the sensors and electronics. Equipped with sensors, it will be able to perceive its environment and showcase some autonomous behavior in the future. 

We see this challenge as both a unique learning opportunity and the creation of a novel research platform. By combining efficiency, agility, and compactness, Equilibrio pushes the boundaries of mobile robotics.

Name: Sebotics
Description: Unser Ziel ist es, das Leben der Menschen mit Robotertechnik nachhaltig zu erleichtern. So sollen Dienstleister, Servicefachkräfte usw. wieder Zeit für den Kunden haben - der Roboter erledigt den Rest.

Name: LEVA Robotics
Description:
LEVA is an all-terrain, autonomous legged robot, being developed by our team of 12 engineers and industrial designers from ETH Zürich, ZHAW and ZHdK.
Our goal is to design a robot that carries standardised containers with heavy payloads in them, over stairs, unpaved land and all kinds of challenging terrain.

We are a focus project at ETH Zürich, supported by the Robotic Systems Lab. Follow us for updates about our project, and don't miss the Focus Rollout on the 28th May 2024, where we will present a fully functional prototype.

- autonomous navigation in extreme indoor and outdoor scenarios (firefighting)

Name: Venture Robot Solutions
Description:
Venture Robot Solutions (VRS) builds a hardware-agnostic, human-aware intelligence layer that enables service robots to behave appropriately around people in real care environments.

Our software focuses on socially acceptable robot behavior, allowing robots to understand social context, navigate shared spaces safely, and interact appropriately with staff, patients, and residents.

VRS solutions are designed to be embedded into existing service robots, improving acceptance, safety, and operational efficiency without changing hardware.

We collaborate with academic and care partners in Switzerland to test and validate our technology in hospitals and elderly care facilities, with a strong focus on measurable impact on workload, safety, and user trust.

Name: Auto-Mate Robotics
Description:
We believe that affordable automation is essential for your SME to stay competitive and keep the production in Switzerland.
We provide a single smart and flexible robotic solution that can be quickly and easily reprogrammed for your different tasks, reducing the cost of the overall processes.
Thanks to a smart and flexible robotic cell, it is possible to integrate any piece of hardware into a single and intuitive interface that can be rapidly and easily re-programmed by your workers.

Name: AutoBike
Description:
Autobike is a student-driven project at ETH Zurich aiming to design and build a self-driving bicycle that can return to its station autonomously. Our mission is to merge mechanical engineering, robotics, and intelligent control systems to create a sustainable and accessible mobility solution for the cities of tomorrow.

We are a multidisciplinary team of 10 students, combining expertise in mechanical design, electronics, software, and control. Over the next year, we will develop a fully functional prototype capable of autonomous navigation, safe braking, and intelligent steering – bringing new possibilities to urban transport and shared mobility.

Our project is supported by academic guidance and inspired by real-world applications: imagine a bike that drops you off at your destination and rides itself back, reducing clutter and making shared mobility seamless.

Name: NOCTUA
Description:
We are a team of engineers from ETH Zürich, supported by the Soft Robotics Lab. Our objective is to engineer a silent long-endurance drone that can autonomously monitor vast areas, supporting rangers in preserving wildlife.
We‘ve successfully completed various test flights and proven our systems airworthiness. 

Currently we are working on making our plane more reliable, modular and efficient. If you would like to contribute, feel free to reach out!

Name: coprod LLC
Description: Making Hardware Simple

Name: Innovationsprojekt pd|z ETH Zürich
Description: The innovation project is a compulsory course in the third semester of the bachelor’s program in Mechanical Engineering at ETH Zurich. During the project, students work in small groups to develop an autonomous robot designed to solve a specific challenge. The task changes from year to year but always presents students with challenging technical problems to solve. The aim of the innovation project is to give students hands-on experience with agile product development methodology. In the final week of the semester, students present the systems they have built and pit them against each other in the public finale in the main building of ETH Zurich.

Name: Demaurex SA
Description:
Our robotic cells orchestrate every piece of equipment across the primary and secondary packaging zones — around a single focus: your product.
Demaurex SA — Delta robot pioneer since 1988. A Swiss family-owned SME, founded in 1983 in Romanel and now headquartered in Vufflens-la-Ville, Switzerland. We design high-throughput pick & place robotic cells for the food industry (chocolate, biscuits, bakery, pastry, ready meals) and the pharmaceutical sector.
Our signature: end-to-end mastery, from the Delta robot — patented at EPFL Lausanne in 1988, the very year we acquired it — to Gemini, our proprietary software that drives every line, whatever the equipment brand, from bare product to ready-to-ship carton.
More than 3,000 robots installed worldwide. 70 team members. Forty years of in-house technical expertise. Our machines are built to run for 20 years — and we keep them running for another 20, with spare parts, retrofits and Gemini updates across every generation we have ever produced.
Now more independent than ever, we are strengthening our customer proximity: short lead times, parts on the shelf, engineers you can actually reach.
www.demaurex.com

Name: Exclaim Robotics
Description:
We build robots to maintain AI data centers.

Just about everything else in a data center is software-controlled,but when a part fails, someone still has to work directly on the rack. With the new generation of AI data centers moving to 800V DC in the rack, that becomes a question of safety, and we think robots are the answer.
We focus specifically on dexterous manipulation problems rather than heavy lifting: cleaning and replacing optics, reconnecting copper cabling, and re-seating drives precisely.

Name: POLARIS - ARIS focus project
Description: The aim of this project is to develop a modular, scalable, remotely observed swarm of underwater robots capable of performing real-time data collection and coordinated actions across a broad range of environments. Unlike fully autonomous systems, our robots will initially focus on proving practical feasibility within our limited timeframe and resources, while keeping open the possibility for future autonomous functionalities. This will involve building working prototypes and iterating on current research in underwater swarm communication and control.

Name: Serenity Robotics
Description:
Our team
Serenity consists of ten highly motivated undergraduate students specializing in mechanical and electrical engineering. We are  supported by Prof. Dr. Marco Hutter and experienced tutors from the Robotics Systems Lab. We want to continue the legacy of pioneering space projects such as Spacehopper and  Spacebok which have been greatly supported by the Euorpean Space Agency (ESA). 

Our mission
We want to develop a versatile platform for future extraterrestrial exploration on the moon.  We envision an easily deployable robotic system capable of withstanding significant impacts and navigating challenging terrains. Our robot will be able to fall from great heights, making deployments cheaper and more successful. The robot adapts to various mission objectives, for example the exploration of lunar caves. These caves are believed to harbor valuable resources like ice and provide protection from radiation, dust, meteorites and temperature fluctuations. If we want to stay at the moon, we first must explore the lunar caves, which could be ideal for future human habitats.

Name: H-Robotics Switzerland
Description:
We provide professional robotic solutions that redefine efficiency, consistency, and quality across industries — from hospitality and retail to healthcare, education, and beyond.

Our range of intelligent cleaning and service robots seamlessly integrates into existing operations, helping teams focus on high-value tasks while improving customer satisfaction and ensuring best-in-class service.

Join the automation revolution and discover how our award-winning robots can elevate your business.

Name: Maus Robotics
Description: Maus Robotics builds intelligent, human-centered robots that bring automation into everyday life. Rooted in Swiss precision and creative design, we pioneer fresh food automation, starting with robots that prepare crêpes in under two minutes.

Name: ASIRA
Description:
We are a focus project team of 8 ETH Zürich engineers committed to advancing smarter, greener industrial technologies for a more efficient future.
ASIRA is our next-generation robotic innovation, designed to physically adapt to a variety of tasks while maximizing energy efficiency. Our vision is to transform industrial robots from rigid, task-specific machines into intelligent, adaptive systems. Inspired by nature, ASIRA dynamically adjusts its configuration to meet diverse task demands, from delicate assemblies to rapid operations, all while prioritizing energy efficiency.
By leveraging AI, ASIRA bridges the gap between hardware and software, enabling quick, autonomous adaptation and optimization. This revolution in automation sets new standards in precision, flexibility, and sustainability.

Name: Zurich Robotics Roundtable
Description:
The Zurich Robotics Roundtable is a new meetup series for robotics founders, operators, researchers, and investors. Our goal is to foster real conversations, share hard-won lessons, and strengthen the robotics community in Zurich.

Want to get involved? Reach out if you're interested in speaking, sponsoring, or helping us organize future events!

Join us on Discord: https://discord.gg/HvY7Svtz

Name: Déploya
Description:
Déploya addresses high safety risks, long installation times, and frequent errors associated with conventional scaffolding systems that rely heavily on manual work.

We developed a fast-deployable vertical grid used primarily for the installation of ventilated façades and cladding systems. The grid is based on origami folding and self-assembling principles, enabling rapid deployment and incorporating integrated rails for mobile robotic tools. This allows the automation of key façade tasks such as marking, drilling, and potentially full panel assembly.

Name: AATB
Description:
AATB – Andrea Anner and Thibault Brevet – is an artist duo investigating human-machine interactions through robotics and industrial automation beyond factory settings. Their practice integrates software programming, electronics, mechanical engineering, and precision machining to critically explore how robotics enters everyday life. Live and work in Zurich and Marseille.

Their work has been exhibited at ZKM (Karlsruhe), V&A Dundee, Ars Electronica (Linz), Chengdu Biennale, New Museum (New York), Venice Architecture Biennale, Zollverein (Essen), Unfold X (Seoul), APS Museum (Shanghai), HEK (Basel), Istanbul Design Biennial, Milan Design Week, and Museum für Gestaltung (Zürich). They have held residencies at CERN and Atelier Luma (Arles) and received the Swiss Design Award in 2021.

AATB has taught at most Swiss art and design universities (ZHDK, ECAL, HEAD, FHNW, HKB, SUPSI) and internationally at Seoul University of the Arts, Design Academy Eindhoven, HFG Karlsruhe, and Iceland University of the Arts. They have lectured at conferences in Tokyo, Prague, The Hague, Seoul, Madrid, Berlin, Cannes, and Turin.

Backed by a top-tier education from ETH Switzerland, 20 years of extensive professional experience, a broad network, and meticulously structured approaches, we consistently provide high-quality solutions.

Name: Sciquoia AG
Description: At Sciquoia AG, we revolutionize pharmaceutical quality control by providing cutting-edge automation solutions for GMP-regulated laboratories. Our pre-qualified, off-the-shelf systems enhance precision, reduce human error, and ensure compliance, streamlining QC workflows for faster, more efficient, and scalable drug manufacturing processes.

Name: Raven Intelligent Systems
Description:
Raven Intelligent Systems is building robotic site intelligence for high-risk worksites.

Most construction sites still operate with fragmented visibility: manual inspections, fixed cameras, drone footage, disconnected reports and issues that are often documented too late. The result is costly blind spots around safety, security, materials and site progress.

Raven turns this fragmented visibility into active site evidence.

By combining cameras, drones and AI, Raven helps site teams detect, verify and document what is happening on site — from severe safety risks and after-hours intrusions to exposed materials, theft exposure and changing 3D site status.

Unlike passive camera systems, safety-only AI alerts or hardware-heavy robots, Raven delivers adaptive coverage and decision-ready evidence reports. Fixed and mobile sensing are orchestrated around priority zones, risk areas and changing site conditions, giving teams broader visibility without adding inspection workload.

Our mission is to help construction leaders act earlier, reduce blind spots and prevent critical risks from escalating into accidents, thefts, material losses, delays or disputes.

Raven is defining a new category: robotic site intelligence — from passive site visibility to active site evidence.

Name: Learn Robotics with ROS
Description:
Learn Robotics with ROS is a robotics engineering education platform focused on helping students, engineers, technicians, universities and companies build real robotic applications.

We teach practical workflows that go beyond isolated ROS2 tutorials:

Simulation → Motion Planning → Vision → Docker → Real Robot Deployment

Our goal is to help learners move from fragmented examples to complete robotics engineering skills that can be applied to real industrial automation tasks.

Core topics include:

• ROS2 software architecture
• MoveIt motion planning and robot manipulation
• Gazebo / simulation-based development
• Computer vision and camera integration
• Docker for robotics deployment
• Real robot applications with 6-axis robots
• Vision-guided pick-and-place workflows
• Simulation-to-real deployment strategy

The learning path starts in simulation, so no robot is required to begin. Students can build foundations with a computer running Ubuntu, then gradually move toward cameras, grippers, Jetson platforms and real robot deployment.

Learn Robotics with ROS is designed for:

• Students who want to become robotics engineers
• Engineers and technicians who want practical robotics skills
• Companies looking for applied robotics training
• Universities and professors building modern robotics programs
• System integrators interested in ROS2, vision and deployment workflows
• Founders developing robotics and automation products

Typical applications include pick-and-place, vision-guided manipulation, machine tending, bin picking concepts, inspection workflows and industrial robotics software architecture.

We do not teach ROS2 as an isolated tool.

We teach the complete engineering workflow required to design, simulate and deploy real robotic systems.
